registry.toolScreenshotDesc: F1 freezes the screen for region capture and annotation (rect/ellipse/arrow/pen/marker/text/mosaic), then copy, save or pin back; F3 pins the clipboard image on screen

screenshot.noClipboardImage: No image in the clipboard. Copy an image first, or press F1 to capture one
screenshot.subtitle: F1 freezes the screen for drag-select capture; annotate, then copy / save / pin it back. F3 pins the clipboard image on your desktop.
screenshot.hotkeyGlobalHint: Hotkeys are global: they work while the app is minimized to the tray. Click a key to re-record; press Backspace to disable.
screenshot.guideCapture: Press the hotkey to freeze the screen, then drag to select a region. Press Enter without selecting to copy the whole screen.
screenshot.guideAnnotate: Once a region is selected a toolbar appears: rectangle, ellipse, arrow, pen, marker, text and mosaic, with 8 colors and 3 stroke widths, plus undo/redo.
screenshot.guideConfirm: Enter or Ctrl+C copies to the clipboard and closes; Ctrl+S saves as PNG; F3 pins the region onto the screen.
screenshot.guideEsc: Esc and right-click step back: text input → annotation tool → selection → capture.
screenshot.keyPin: Pin the region onto the screen
screenshot.keyNudge: Nudge the selection by pixels (hold Shift to speed up)
screenshot.pinGuide1: Drag to move, scroll to zoom around the cursor; the context menu has copy / save as / reset zoom.
screenshot.pinGuide2: Double-click or press Esc to close a pin; consecutive pins are offset from each other.
screenshot.pinGuide3: F3 pins the image currently in the clipboard: copy an image in any app, then press F3.
screenshot.hint: Enter copy · Ctrl+S save · F3 pin · Ctrl+Z undo · Esc cancel
screenshot.noticeBody: Global hotkeys are now active: {capture} to capture, {pin} to pin the clipboard image — they work in any app. Change or disable them on the Screenshot tool page.
